name_en: Rokubee — noodles made from sweet potato starch, served in a clear dashi broth
summary_ja: さつまいもの粉末を山芋でつないでうどん状にし、すまし汁で食べる麺料理。1792年の眉山崩壊による飢饉の際、深江村の六兵衛という人が保存食のさつまいも粉を使って考案したのが始まりと伝わる。
summary_en: Sweet potato starch bound with grated mountain yam is shaped into thick noodles and served in a clear broth — said to have been devised by a man named Rokubee in Fukae village after the 1792 Mount Mayu collapse triggered a famine, using preserved sweet potato flour.
source_title: ろくべえ／六兵衛 長崎県

name_en: Sara udon — noodles fried and topped with a thick vegetable-and-meat sauce, eaten with vinegar and Worcester sauce
summary_ja: ちゃんぽんと同じ具材を使い、太麺を汁がなくなるまで炒めるか、細く揚げた麺に五目あんかけをかける麺料理。1899年、ちゃんぽんを考案した中華料理店の店主が汁なしのちゃんぽんとしてつくったのが始まりとされる。
summary_en: Using the same toppings as champon, thick noodles are fried until dry or crisp thin noodles are draped in a mixed-vegetable gravy — said to have begun in 1899, when the same restaurant owner who created champon made a broth-free version of it.

name_ja: 地獄炊き（五島うどん・島原そうめん）
name_en: Jigoku-daki — five island udon or Shimabara somen boiled and eaten straight from an iron pot with flying-fish dashi
summary_ja: 乾麺の五島うどんを鉄鍋でぐつぐつと茹で、トビウオでとった「あごだし」につけて食べる食べ方。遣唐使が製法を伝えたとの説がある五島の特産麺で、島原そうめんも同様に薬味でゆでたてを楽しむという。
summary_en: Dried five-island udon noodles are boiled bubbling in an iron pot and dipped in ago-dashi, a broth made from flying fish — a way of eating this Goto specialty noodle, said by one theory to have arrived with envoys to Tang China; Shimabara somen is enjoyed hot the same way.
source_title: 地獄炊き（五島うどん・島原そうめん） 長崎県
